study type: Cross-sectional survey with a discrete choice experiment
exposure: risk of death of the newborn
outcome: women's preferences for water immersion during labor and birth
cohort: 1088 women who completed an online survey exploring preferences for water immersion during labor and birth, some of whom had prior childbirth experience.
finding: The risk of death of the newborn was given high priority by women when considering water immersion, while the risk of severe perineal tears was considered the least important attribute.
mod_finding: Preferences for water birth varied among women, with the largest group (52.9%) interested if it reduced pain and was risk-free for the newborn, another group (30.8%) interested only during the labor phase, and a third group (16.2%) not interested in water immersion at all.
